title: Most Agent Calls Are Decisions, Not Generation

questions.prompt: Which of these prompts is a decision call?
options: Summarize this issue in three sentences
Classify this issue as bug, feature, or question
Write a fix for this issue
questions.explanation: Classification has a closed set of three legal answers, so it is a decision. The others produce open-ended text whose length and content vary, which is generation. 'Write a fix' is tempting because it is short work, but 'short' and 'closed set' are different things.

questions.prompt: A prompt asks for 'yes/no, plus a one-line reason.' How do you classify it?
options: Decision, because yes/no is a closed set
Generation, because the reason section is open-ended — ask for the label only to make it a decision
It depends only on the model size
questions.explanation: The free-text reason reopens the output, so the call generates as well as decides. Split it: ask for the label as a decision, and log the reason separately if you need it. The tempting answer stops at 'yes/no' and misses that one open-ended field undoes the closed set.

questions.prompt: A loop spends 80% of its budget on decision calls run through a frontier model. What is the best first move?
options: Route the decision calls to a cheaper decision model or tier
Ask the model for shorter answers
questions.explanation: The problem is a mismatch between the task (pick from a list) and the meter (frontier generation). Moving the decisions to a cheaper tier attacks the mismatch. 'Shorter answers' is tempting but only trims output tokens while you still pay frontier input and overhead on a closed question.

questions.prompt: Which call is NOT a good candidate to move to a cheaper decision tier?
options: Pick which of five tools to call next
Score this paragraph's relevance from 0 to 3
Write the user-facing changelog for this release
Answer whether this build log contains an error
questions.explanation: A changelog is open-ended prose — the output can be any string — so it is generation and needs the stronger model. The other three all have closed output sets (a tool, a score, a yes/no) and are safe to move down. The tempting trap is that a changelog entry can be short, but shortness is not a closed set.
